synopsis: UNECE GRVA’s January 2024 document GRVA-18-55 found that the proposal to add virtual testing to UN Regulation 152 for AEB did not address every identified aspect of credible virtual-testing capability [f1279, f7144]. The corpus treats this as independent regulatory-working-group evidence that credibility requirements remained unresolved at that point, even for on-road AEB [f1280, f7145]. A draft UN Global Technical Regulation on automated driving systems, discussed at GRVA workshops in March and June 2025, builds a harmonised credibility framework covering toolchain management, requirements, verification and validation; the supplied facts do not establish that it resolves the earlier R152 gaps [f10598, f1279]. For planning, the corpus contrasts vendor claims of replacing substantial physical testing with formal sources—including GRVA—that frame simulation as complementary and require qualified models [f1971].

relations.note: Both report the January 2024 R152 proposal's incomplete coverage of virtual-testing credibility.
Identified omissions underpin the chapter's interpretation that AEB virtual-testing credibility remained insufficient.
Incomplete credibility coverage underpins the warning that regulatory details remain unsettled.
Both interpret the January 2024 critique as evidence of unresolved on-road virtual-testing credibility.
The later ADS draft specifies credibility-framework components, without establishing resolution of R152 gaps.
Regulatory concern about credibility supports caution toward vendor claims of replacing physical testing.
